dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: Yes, there's a fairy in this spring. You wouldn't have heard of it, and none of the villagers believe in it.

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: But when I was a boy, I would talk to her here all the time...

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: We'd talk about the weather, the spring water, the fish, who had fallen out with who in the village...

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: And when a kid fell into the spring, she'd tell me how she had secretly helped them back out and given them a few pretty stones to make them feel better...

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: But suddenly, one day, she refused to see me any longer.

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: So... what are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: How many years now... thirty? No — forty?

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: Well anyway, it's been half a lifetime that I've waited here, just hoping to see her one last time... and to hear her wonderful, flowing voice...

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: But after all this time, I'm sure she's probably... gone...

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: Whenever I have that thought, I realize... Look how old I am now... Too old to go traveling around Teyvat looking for her...

dialogues.speaker: Old Finch
dialogues.text: So all I can do is wait here, on the off chance that there's still some hope.
